title: Jaston Williams' UFO-focused play I Saw the Lights opens next week at Tobin Center
excerpt: I Saw the Lights was inspired by the mass UFO sightings over Lubbock in 1951. The mainstage season for the Tobin Center's in-house theater company, 100A
content:
The mainstage season for the Tobin Center’s in-house theater company, 100A Productions, opens Wednesday, Sept. 16, with I Saw the Lights, written by and starring Jaston Williams and directed by Chris McGarry (The Sopranos).

Inspired by the infamous mass UFO sightings over Lubbock in 1951, this re-envisioned multi-character play explores how different people interpret singular events according to their individual beliefs, predispositions and deeply personal recollections.

Williams — co-creator, co-writer and longtime star of Greater Tuna and its sequels — is joined by a stellar group of local thespians who bring both humor and wonder to the stage for this series of performances.

$24.50-$47.50, check website for showtimes Wednesday, Sept. 16-Sunday, Sept. 27, Tobin Center for the Performing Arts, 100 Auditorium Circle, (210) 223-8624, tobincenter.org.
